scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Aaliyah Washington and I'm 43. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Aaliyah. I'm sorry to hear about the frustration regarding this charge, especially after you've been traveling. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide the email address associated with your account and the last four digits of the payment method used?
Sure, the email is a.washington@email.com and the card ends in 4492.
Thank you for that information. I have located your account. For security, could you please confirm the billing zip code on file?

Thank you, Aaliyah. I have verified your account. I can see the cancellation request was processed 34 days ago. While our 'Service Agreement Section 4.2' states that refunds must be requested within 30 days of the renewal date, I understand your situation regarding your travel. I am going to make a one-time exception to our policy and process this refund for you.
Oh, that is such a relief! Thank you so much for understanding.

You are very welcome! I have successfully processed the refund of $49.99 back to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit appear in your bank account within 3-5 business days. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?
No, that was everything. Thanks again for the help.
It was my pleasure, Aaliyah. Thank you for being a valued customer, and I hope you have a wonderful rest of your week!

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account details and, citing Service Agreement Section 4.2, granted a one-time exception to the 30-day refund policy.
